Messages.Author: Colin McGuigan
Messages.Body:
vermillian wrote:
> These fill certain niches that your 'staple' cards would typically
> fill, yet are different. Some have texts a bit lengthy... Some have
> power levels I'm not entirely sure about.

Auspex needs more variety amongst its inferiors than "+1 intercept".

A lot of the cards are pretty damn powerful: Empathic Reaction. Neutral
Form is horrendously powerful for the [!]Malks. (+2 stealth, Neutral
Form, as many bleed modifiers as I can lay down.). Monster from the
Woods. Poisonous Touch. Superior Impressive Stance. Frickin' superior
Fearful Might. Jesus. Mmmm. Rage of Hell. This Meeting Will Adjourn.

I like how a lot of the nullferiors are conditional, but some of the
more basic ones probably shouldn't be -- eg, a rush card, etc.

I don't understand Antagonizing the Beast's superior.

Nullferior Theft of Freedom is _way_ too weak. Arguably, the sup and
inf should be flipped, too.

For is...eh. There's very little diversity. Maybe to be expected, but
I kept thinking I was looking at the same card over and over.

Is Provisional Stamina "a" combat card, as in singular, or all combat cards?

Earthen Shield: pro, I assume should read "up to one agg damage"? The
for+pro is nice.

Inner Focus: Why first strike?

Cult Follower's wording is odd.

Mmm. I'm seeing a lot of combat. Just off the top of my head, first
deck I'd do would be Lasombra obt/pot/dom. pot/dom both have cards that
force opponents to burn blood to block, and then I just smack the
bejeezus out of them with the pot strikes/pot+obt additional strike.
Meanwhile, superior Impressive Stance means they can't do nothing but
hands for 1. They don't block, they get bled for bunches.

Alternatively, cel/pre. Pre bleed (at some stealth, no less), and lots
of Bullet Dodger.

Interesting variety, though, for excluded. Good start.

--Colin McGuigan
